newsitem.title: USA: WMX considers Wessex, ServiceMaster sales.
newsitem.headline: WMX considers Wessex, ServiceMaster sales.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc said it is considering the possible sale of its interests in ServiceMaster LP and Wessex Water Plc, but not before 1998.

"These are options being considered and discussed ... But we cannot do anything until 1998 under our agreements with both companies. We would not proceed without their approval and cooperation," said WMX spokesman Bill Plunkett.
Rumors that Oak Brook, Ill.-based WMX was eyeing the sale of Wessex Water, a U.K. water utility, were reported in the British press earlier this year.
Plunkett said analysts have discussed the possible sale of WMX's stake in ServiceMaster, an Illinois cleaning services firm, for months. "This is kind of old news," he said.

WMX has recently sold off water-related businesses, an industrial scaffolding business, medical wastes operations and other interests. "This Wessex and Servicemaster issue is part of a larger monetizaton issue in which we are disposing of non-core or non-performing assets," Plunkett said.
WMX is one of the world's largest trash-handling concerns. It owns about 19 percent of ServiceMaster, whose shares were up 1/8 to 26. WMX also owns a one-fifth stake in Wessex.
If the stakes were sold, WMX could make substantial gains. "You're getting up near the billion-dollar range," said Edward Jones analyst William Fiala.
He speculated that WMX might sell its stakes in the two companies when it is able to do so.
"What they've been doing internally recently is simplifying the business structure. This would make sense and they do have quite a bit of debt," Fiala said.
